title: Ada and the Choir
premise: Casper Thackeray, a temple scribe indentured by his father's debts, has spent years mapping the smuggler roads through the Thornfell mountains in exchange for quiet survival. When the crown declares a hunt for anyone bearing the old gift of soul-song, Casper discovers he carries it too — and that the temple he serves has been selling gifted souls to the court beneath the mountain for generations. Fleeing with Ada, a mute child whose soul was already sold, and a disgraced choir mistress named Wren, he must reach the court before midwinter seals its gates and steal Ada's soul back. He succeeds only by offering his own voice in trade, but Ada — who has learned to sing without sound — gives it back to him, breaking the court's claim on both their bloodlines.
about_author: Petra Fairweather is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing medieval choir manuscripts before turning to fiction. She writes fantasy about debt, music, and the families we build when inheritance fails us.

chapters.title: The Ledger of Small Debts
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. In the mountain temple of Thornfell, Casper copies prayers by candlelight while calculating how many winters remain on his father's debt. A routine errand to the archive reveals a second ledger — one recording souls, not coin. Emotional beat: the unease of a man who suspects his safe life is built on something rotten.

chapters.title: What the Bell Cannot Say
chapters.summary: Ada's POV, rendered in close third through her gestures and drawings. The temple's foundling, Ada watches the priests measure children for 'aptitude' and hides the hum she feels in her chest. She witnesses another child taken below. Emotional beat: terror sharpening into resolve as she decides to run before her turn comes.

chapters.title: A Hunt Proclaimed
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. Crown riders arrive with a decree: all bearers of the gift must surrender themselves for 'sanctification.' The abbot's hands shake as he signs the proclamation, and Casper realizes the temple will comply eagerly — because compliance hides its own crimes. Emotional beat: dread curdling into betrayal.

chapters.title: The Smuggler's Road
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. Casper finds Ada hiding in the salt cellars and makes a split-second choice: he uses his knowledge of the smuggler roads to slip them both out ahead of the riders. First use of his gift — a whispered note that stills a guard dog. Emotional beat: exhilaration shadowed by fear of what he just revealed himself to be.

chapters.title: Wren of the Broken Choir
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. In the lowland town of Marrowgate, Wren — once choir mistress to a royal chapel, now drunk and disgraced — recognizes the gift in Casper when he hums to warm his hands. She offers to teach him control in exchange for passage north. Emotional beat: two survivors recognizing each other's damage.

chapters.title: Lessons in Borrowed Voices
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. On the road, Wren teaches Casper the discipline of soul-song: every note given costs memory or warmth. Ada, unable to speak, demonstrates an impossible technique — singing silently, spending nothing. Emotional beat: wonder, and Wren's grief for the choir she lost.

chapters.title: The Price on Our Heads
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. Bounty notices appear with Casper's face sketched from a temple informant's memory. A near-capture at a river ford forces him to spend a cherished memory of his mother to blind the hunters. Emotional beat: the first true payment of survival's price, and resentment at having to pay it.

chapters.title: Ashes of the Chapel Royal
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Passing the burned ruin of Wren's old chapel, she confesses why she fell from grace: she refused to send her choristers below the mountain, and the crown made an example of her. One chorister survived — sold anyway. Emotional beat: guilt transmuted into fierce protectiveness toward Ada.

chapters.title: The Court Beneath
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. An old smuggler, Brannoc, tells them the truth of the court beneath Thornfell: a subterranean realm where souls are currency, ruled by the Pale Cantor, and sealed against entry until midwinter — after which no one enters or leaves until spring. Emotional beat: the ticking clock becomes real; hope and horror in equal measure.

chapters.title: What Ada Remembers
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Through drawings by firelight, Ada reveals she remembers being below once — that her mother traded her soul to buy passage out, and that somewhere beneath lives a woman who may be her mother still. Emotional beat: longing complicated by anger; Ada wants her soul back but fears what else she'll find.

chapters.title: The Toll Bridge at Greywater
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. The last bridge before the mountain is guarded by a toll-keeper who trades in memories instead of coin. To cross, Wren surrenders the memory of her choir's final concert — the last beautiful thing she owned. Emotional beat: sacrifice freely chosen, and the group becoming a family rather than fellow travelers.

chapters.title: Hunters in the Snow
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. The crown's chief hunter, Serah Vail — herself a gifted woman who bought safety by serving the crown — corners them in a whiteout. Wren duels her with song while Casper and Ada escape upward. Emotional beat: Wren's capture, and the crushing weight of leaving her behind.

chapters.title: The Cave of First Notes
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. Sheltering in a cavern where the mountain itself resonates, Casper learns the gift's origin: the mountain was once sung into being, and the court below is its corrupted echo. Ada's silent song harmonizes with the stone, opening a crack in the rock no one else can pass. Emotional beat: awe, and the realization that Ada is not broken but extraordinary.

chapters.title: Descent
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. They enter the court beneath the mountain: a cathedral vastness where stolen souls hang like lanterns, each flickering with the life it once held. Casper finds the ledger of souls and locates Ada's entry — purchased by the Pale Cantor personally. Emotional beat: revulsion and vertigo; the scale of the theft is beyond anything he imagined.

chapters.title: The Pale Cantor
chapters.summary: The Cantor's POV. The ruler of the court receives them with terrible courtesy, revealing that Casper's own father sold a soul here long ago — Casper's sister's. The Cantor offers a bargain: Ada's soul for Casper's voice, forever. Emotional beat: seduction and horror; the Cantor is reasonable, which makes him worse.

chapters.title: Serah's Choice
chapters.summary: Serah Vail's POV. Brought below as the Cantor's hunter, Serah confronts Wren in the soul-vaults and learns what the Cantor truly does with harvested souls: he eats them to hold back the mountain's hunger. Serah realizes she has been feeding children to a starving god. Emotional beat: the collapse of her justification, and her turn toward rebellion.

chapters.title: The Bargain Struck
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. Midwinter approaches; the gates begin to close. Casper agrees to the trade — his voice for Ada's soul — believing it the only way. As the Cantor draws out his song, Casper spends every remaining memory of his father willingly, emptying himself of the debt that defined him. Emotional beat: liberation inside loss.

chapters.title: The Silent Song
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Voiceless Casper cannot leave — the gate requires a song to open. But Ada has spent the whole journey learning to sing without spending anything, and now she sings the gate open with her silent song, then reaches into the Cantor's hoard and pulls Casper's voice free, giving it back. Emotional beat: the found family's love overturning the logic of sacrifice.

chapters.title: The Mountain Wakes
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs converging. Freed souls pour out of the vaults as the mountain remembers its original song; the Cantor, starved of his hoard, dissolves into the stone he came from. Serah holds the gates open while Wren leads the freed souls upward in chorus. Emotional beat: catharsis — centuries of theft undone in a single rising chord.

chapters.title: Reckoning at Thornfell
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. They return to the temple with proof of the soul-ledger. The abbot falls; the debt-records burn; Casper walks out owing nothing to anyone. Serah departs to testify to the crown, carrying evidence that may end the hunt. Emotional beat: justice without triumphalism — the cost is counted honestly.

chapters.title: A Choir of the Unowned
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. In Marrowgate, Wren founds a new choir of the freed and the gifted, teaching the silent song so no one need ever pay in memory again. Ada takes her place among the singers, and finds among them a woman with her mother's eyes — alive, imperfect, unready. Emotional beat: reunion deferred but possible; healing begun, not finished.

chapters.title: The Long Winter Ends
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. On the first day of spring, Casper climbs the Thornfell road one last time — not as a debtor or a fugitive but as a free man — and sings the mountain's first note back to it. Ada joins him, silent and radiant. Emotional beat: quiet joy; the price of survival was paid, but inheritance is rewritten, and family is what remains.
